title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Context: on the previous page Grothendieck conjectures a Tannakian-type equivalence. On one side are representations of the prime-to-p (or L-) fundamental group, possibly a relative pro-group over S. On the other are modules with 'integrable' stratification on X. Here 'integrable' means a stratified module (a crystal on the infinitesimal or HPD site) that becomes trivial on a finite étale, prime-to-p covering, i.e. one that 'comes from' a representation of pi_1^{(p')}. Item 4) treats the rank-one case. Setting: X of finite type over a field k, geometrically unibranch; the margin asks 'loc. de t.f. suffit?'. Claim: an invertible stratified module L is integrable iff there is n>0, prime to p, with L^{⊗n} isomorphic to (O_X, trivial stratification). Equivalently, the class of L is torsion of order prime to p in the group of stratified invertible modules. The 'if' direction holds without unibranchness: the Kummer cover Spec(⊕_{i<n} L^{⊗-i}) is finite étale of degree n and trivialises L. A first necessary condition is therefore that [L] is torsion prime to p in Pic(X). Once L^{⊗n} ≅ O_X as a module, it remains to decide which stratifications on O_X are integrable. Characteristic 0 (margin 'ici car. 0 !'), X presumably smooth: stratifications on O_X correspond to flat connections d+ω with ω a closed 1-form. Isomorphisms act by ω ↦ ω + df/f for f a unit, so the connection is trivial iff ω is a logarithmic differential df/f with f in Γ(X,O_X^*). Hence the connection is integrable iff nω is logarithmic for some n>0, i.e. it has finite monodromy. By Rosenlicht, the group dlog Γ(X,O^*) ≅ Γ(X,O^*)/k^* is free of finite rank r: L ≅ Z^r. The next page concludes that the group of integrable connections on O_X up to isomorphism is L⊗Q/Z ≅ (Q/Z)^r. When X is complete (units constant) only the trivial one is integrable. In arbitrary characteristic, if global units are horizontal, the only integrable stratification on O_X is the trivial one. So integrable stratified line bundles are then classified by prime-to-p torsion line bundles.
errors: The identification 'stratifications on O_X = flat connections = closed 1-forms' in char 0 requires X smooth (or a suitable replacement on singular X); the page only assumes finite type plus geometrically unibranch.

Rosenlicht's theorem gives Γ(X,O^*)/k^* finitely generated. Freeness (and the rank r) needs X geometrically connected and reduced, and should be read over k algebraically closed or with geometric hypotheses. This is not stated.

The role of the geometric unibranch hypothesis in the 'only if' direction is not justified on the page. It is presumably needed for the comparison with pi_1 (connectedness of étale covers / horizontal sections being constant).

ideas.what: Integrable stratification = stratified module trivialised by a finite étale (prime-to-p) covering, i.e. coming from a representation of pi_1^{(p')}; rank-one case: torsion of order prime to p in the group of stratified line bundles, via Kummer coverings
ideas.modern_name: stratified bundles with finite (prime-to-p) monodromy; essentially finite stratified bundles
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gieseker (1975) for stratified bundles and pi_1 in char p; dos Santos (2007); Esnault–Mehta; Kindler (finite monodromy)
ideas.where_published: Stratifications appear in Grothendieck's 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés) and in Berthelot's work; this precise 'intégrable' notion is unsure

ideas.what: Char 0: rank-one flat connections on O_X with finite monodromy ↔ closed forms ω with nω = dlog f; group of iso classes ≅ (dlog units)⊗Q/Z ≅ (Q/Z)^r via Rosenlicht
ideas.modern_name: torsion rank-one local systems with trivial underlying bundle; Kummer theory of units
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (Deligne, Équations différentielles à points singuliers réguliers, 1970, context); Rosenlicht (1957) for units

ideas.what: If global units are horizontal (e.g. X proper), the only integrable stratification on O_X is trivial, so integrable stratified line bundles = prime-to-p torsion line bundles
ideas.modern_name: rank-one case of comparison between essentially finite stratified bundles and pi_1^et

missed.claim: Together with the previous page, this is an early (c.1972) programme for a relative Tannakian comparison. One side is representations of a prime-to-p (L-) pro-étale fundamental group of X/S; the other is stratified modules on X 'integrable' in the sense of étale-local triviality. The present page works out the rank-one test case. It predates Gieseker's 1975 paper on stratified bundles and pi_1 in char p, but is consistent with later work (dos Santos, Esnault–Mehta, Kindler on finite monodromy). The relative version over a base S seems less developed in the literature.
missed.quote: Je dis que la stratification est intégrable ssi ∃ entier n>0, premier à la car., tel que L^{⊗n} soit trivial comme module stratifié
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents Grothendieck anticipating the stratified-bundle / étale pi_1 dictionary in positive characteristic. The rank-one mathematics itself is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The rank-one computations are elementary (Kummer cover, closed forms modulo dlog of units, Rosenlicht). Their interest is historical: they show Grothendieck c.1972 thinking about stratified modules versus prime-to-p pi_1, a topic later developed by Gieseker, dos Santos and Esnault et al.
transcription_corrections: 'Or, si X est sur Ω_X ... les stratifications sur Ω_X correspondent et bijection' is more plausibly 'Or, si X est lisse (sur k), les stratifications sur O_X correspondent bijectivement aux connexions à courbure nulle, i.e. aux 1-formes fermées sur X'.

'un diviseur logarithmique' / 'le groupe des diviseurs logarithmiques' should likely read 'une différentielle (dérivée) logarithmique' / 'le groupe des différentielles logarithmiques'. The next page speaks of 'dérivée logarithmique'.
The bracket before Rosenlicht is likely '[cf. Rosenlicht]'.
The struck word at the end of the first sentence (after 'stratification intégrable,') is illegible; 'accessible' is doubtful.
'Dire que la stratification (ou la connexion) soit triviale revient à dire que ω est une différentielle logarithmique' is the likely reading of the garbled middle lines.
